```{r}
#| include: false
library(visualbrief)

# Replace with your data, for example:
# campaign <- vb_read_csv("campaign.csv", date = "Day", content = "Ad name",
#                         impressions = "Impressions", clicks = "Link clicks")
campaign <- campaign_demo

# Your visual identity, or vb_brand_yml("_brand.yml")
brand <- vb_brand("Your organisation")
```

## Summary

```{r}
knitr::kable(summary(campaign)[, c("impressions", "clicks", "ctr", "engagement_rate", "conversion_rate")],
             digits = 4)
```

Write here the two or three findings that matter for the decision at hand.

## Results by channel

```{r}
knitr::kable(vb_summarise(campaign, by = "channel")[, c("channel", "impressions", "ctr", "engagement_rate", "cpa")],
             digits = 4)
```

## Which content works with each audience

```{r}
#| fig-height: 7
vb_plot_rates(campaign, metric = "ctr", by = "content", within = "audience", brand = brand)
```

```{r}
cmp <- vb_compare(campaign, metric = "ctr", by = "content", within = "audience")
knitr::kable(cmp[, c("audience", "content", "rate", "diff", "diff_low", "diff_high", "p_adjusted")], digits = 4)
```

## Over time

```{r}
vb_plot_trend(campaign, metric = "ctr", by = "channel", brand = brand)
```

## Notes

Campaign data are observational unless they come from a randomised test.
Differences describe this campaign; they do not prove that one piece causes
better results.
